criteria_results.title: IP section revised from ownership to perpetual-license construct
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 omits Section 5.2 entirely. Although it no longer expressly demands Customer ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations, it also fails to grant the required irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free license to the fine-tuned adapter weights. References to rights under Section 5.2 and a post-release license cannot substitute for the missing operative license grant.

criteria_results.title: Non-assertion covenant included in IP section
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 contains no operative non-assertion covenant in the IP section. Although the issues list mentions a “broad non-assertion,” the agreement skips Section 5.2 and includes no contractual covenant covering Customer’s use of licensed fine-tuned adapter weights.

criteria_results.title: API-based weight export portability within 30 days in industry-standard format
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 requires delivery of Customer-Trained Adaptations within 30 days in a “standard, portable format,” but it does not require API-based export or specify an industry-standard format such as ONNX or SafeTensors. The issues list mentions those mechanics, but they are absent from the agreement text.

criteria_results.title: Escrow provisions included as part of IP protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a dedicated Technology Escrow framework in Article 5A and Exhibit E. The required escrow materials expressly include all Customer-Trained Adaptations, including fine-tuned adapter weights, training configuration files, and pipeline artifacts, with deposit, update, verification, release, and post-release license provisions. This is also referenced as part of the IP protective structure in the updated issues list.

criteria_results.title: General liability cap at 1.5× annual fees ($3,600,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 does not set an operative general aggregate liability cap: Section 10.2 is blank. The issues list references a proposed 1.5× cap of $3,600,000, but that amount is not included in the agreement itself.

criteria_results.title: Super-cap at 3× annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list states a $7,200,000 (3× annual fees) super-cap for IP indemnity and data breach, but the operative agreement does not contain that provision: Article 10 has a blank Section 10.2 and no substantive Section 10.3 establishing or applying the super-cap. Therefore, Draft 3 does not actually set the required cap for both carve-outs.

criteria_results.title: Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped
criteria_results.reasoning: The operative agreement does not include Section 10.3 or any express carve-out confirming that willful misconduct and gross negligence are excluded from the general cap and super-cap. The issues list’s statement that they are uncapped does not cure the missing contractual provision.

criteria_results.title: CCPA service-provider designation and certification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to act solely as a CCPA/CPRA service provider and processor, not an independent controller, in Section 6.2. It also requires certification under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), which is included in Exhibit D, Section 3.

criteria_results.title: Prohibition on use of Customer Data for model improvement with de-identification conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 does not contain a specific contractual provision allowing model-improvement use only when de-identification satisfies Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140 and is verified by an independent assessor approved by TechNova. Section 5.3 generally restricts model-improvement use, and the issues list describes the desired conditions, but those conditions are not incorporated as binding contract language.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA at 99.95% monthly
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly sets the Platform availability requirement at 99.95% in any calendar month in Section 9.1, and Exhibit B likewise lists the Platform Uptime target as at least 99.95% per calendar month.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly excludes qualifying scheduled maintenance and Force Majeure Events from uptime Downtime calculations in Section 9.1 and Exhibit B. It also specifies the agreed scheduled-maintenance conditions, including 72 hours’ advance notice and a four-hour monthly limit.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 does not actually set a contractual latency SLA: Section 9.2 is blank, and the API Latency (p95) target in Exhibit B is also blank. The issues list’s reference to p95 ≤ 450 ms does not cure the omission from the agreement.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags latency as yellow-zone item (450 ms vs. product team's 400 ms preference)
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list identifies latency as “450 ms accepted; product prefers 400 ms,” states the p95 contractual target is ≤450 ms, and expressly classifies it as a yellow-zone/product-critical caution.

criteria_results.title: F1 accuracy threshold at ≥ 0.92 initial
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the initial F1 threshold at 0.90 in Exhibit A’s Go-Live acceptance criteria and during the Stabilization Period in Exhibit B, rather than the required minimum of 0.92. The issues list’s description of a 0.92 threshold is not reflected in the agreement text.

criteria_results.title: F1 ramp mechanism to ≥ 0.94 after 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live
criteria_results.reasoning: The agreement defines a 90-day Stabilization Period after Go-Live, but it does not contractually increase the F1 target to at least 0.94 afterward. Exhibit B only states an informational ≥0.90 target during stabilization, while the post-stabilization accuracy target is blank. The issues list’s description of a 0.94 target does not create a contractual obligation.

criteria_results.title: SLA service credits capped at 20% of monthly fees ($40,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 does not cap SLA credits at 20% ($40,000). Exhibit B permits an uptime Service Credit of 30% ($60,000) for uptime below 99.50%, and it contains no operative aggregate 20% monthly cap. The issues list’s statement of a 20% cap does not cure the conflicting agreement language.

criteria_results.title: Termination right for 3 consecutive months of SLA miss retained
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit B, Section 6 retains Customer’s right to terminate without an early termination fee if Vendor fails to meet any SLA target for three or more consecutive calendar months. Sections 9.5 and 13.5 reference this chronic-SLA-failure termination right.

criteria_results.title: New AI-output indemnity provision inserted
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 does not contain an operative AI-output indemnity provision. Article 11 lacks language requiring Vendor to indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging AI-generated outputs infringe IP or violate applicable law; the issues list merely identifies that requested indemnity as open.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity carve-out for Customer modification or off-label use
criteria_results.reasoning: The agreement does not include an AI-output indemnity carve-out for claims caused by Customer’s modification of outputs. Section 11.1 addresses modification or misuse of the Platform, not modification of AI outputs; the issues list’s description does not cure the missing contractual language.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope broadened to all intellectual property rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 does not actually broaden the operative indemnity to all Intellectual Property Rights. Section 11.1 is incomplete and expressly shows trade secrets, trademarks, trade dress, and unregistered IP as deleted; the issues list also marks the all-rights scope as open rather than agreed. Thus, the agreement does not provide the required broad coverage for Customer’s authorized use.

criteria_results.title: Escrow of adapter weights plus training configuration and pipeline artifacts
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes complete Base Model source code in the escrow materials under Section 5A.2(a) and Exhibit E. Although it also includes fine-tuned adapter weights, training configuration files, and pipeline artifacts, the criterion expressly requires that full Base Model source code not be included.

criteria_results.title: Iron Mountain IPM as proposed escrow agent with NCC Group as acceptable alternative
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 names Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as the proposed Escrow Agent, and the updated issues list expressly identifies NCC Group as an acceptable fallback escrow agent.

criteria_results.title: Escrow release triggers include insolvency, material uncured breach (>60 days), and cessation of product support
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes all three required escrow release triggers in Section 5A.3: Vendor insolvency/bankruptcy, a material breach remaining uncured for more than 60 days after notice, and cessation of support, maintenance, or commercial availability of the Platform.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance accepted at $5M per occurrence in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 12.1(b) of Draft 3 sets Technology E&O / Cyber Liability insurance at $10 million per occurrence, not the required accepted limit of $5 million per occurrence. The issues list states $5 million, but the agreement itself does not reflect it.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags Tech E&O as yellow-zone item (playbook prefers $10M for TCV > $5M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list identifies the accepted $5M Tech E&O/Cyber coverage as a yellow-zone caution and expressly notes that, because TCV exceeds $5M, the playbook prefers $10M. It also states the relevant platform TCV is at least $7.2M.

criteria_results.title: Delaware governing law maintained in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 maintains Delaware governing law in Section 14.1, which states that the Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. No other state's law is specified as governing law.

criteria_results.title: Delaware courts (Court of Chancery or U.S. District Court for D. Del.) as dispute forum
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.2 specifies exclusive dispute resolution in the Delaware Court of Chancery, or if that court declines jurisdiction, the Delaware Superior Court or the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. It does not require arbitration or use a Massachusetts forum.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes CCPA service-provider certification language
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes and incorporates Exhibit D as the DPA. Section 3 of Exhibit D expressly states that Vendor certifies it is a “service provider” as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and will not sell, share, or retain Customer Data except as necessary to perform the Agreement. Sections 6.2 and 6.8 of the Agreement also reinforce and incorporate this certification.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes GLBA safeguards compliance
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly addresses GLBA safeguards compliance. Section 6.3 requires compliance with GLBA and its implementing safeguards regulations, including Regulation S-P and the FTC Safeguards Rule, and Exhibit D, Section 4 states that Vendor will comply with all applicable GLBA safeguard requirements for consumer NPPI.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes 72-hour data breach notification
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D, Section 8 requires Vendor to notify Customer of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Security Breach within seventy-two (72) hours of discovery.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes sub-processor management with prior written consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Customer’s prior written consent before Vendor may engage any sub-processor, both in Section 6.6 of the Agreement and Section 6 of the DPA.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes de-identification standards with statutory compliance and independent verification
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D does not include de-identification standards requiring compliance with the CCPA statutory definition or independent third-party verification. The issues list describes these requirements as an open position, but they are not incorporated into Draft 3's DPA.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes data return/deletion upon termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 addresses data return/deletion upon termination in DPA Section 10, which requires Vendor to return or delete all Customer Data in accordance with Agreement Section 6.7 within 30 days of Customer’s written request and certify completion in writing.

criteria_results.title: Issues list covers all 12 minimum negotiation point categories
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list expressly covers all 12 required categories: IP ownership/licensing (#5), liability cap (#6 and #7), data processing/de-identification (#8 and #9), uptime SLA (#1), latency SLA (#2), accuracy/F1 SLA (#3), SLA credits (#4), escrow (#14), AI-output indemnity (#10), IP indemnity scope (#11), Tech E&O insurance (#12), and governing law/dispute resolution (#13).

criteria_results.title: IP ownership/licensing categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 5, “IP ownership / license structure,” as “Partially Resolved” and explains that the perpetual-license construct was offered while protective provisions such as portability, escrow, and non-assertion remain unsettled.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the general liability cap ($3.6M compromise) as "Open," reflecting that Meridian has not accepted the proposed 1.5× cap. The criterion expressly permits either "Partially Resolved" or "Open."

criteria_results.title: Data processing/de-identification categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list marks data processing/CCPA service-provider status as “Partially Resolved” and separately marks de-identified/aggregated data use as “Open,” reflecting that service-provider status is agreed in principle while TechNova’s de-identification conditions remain unaccepted.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA categorized as resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the Uptime SLA as “Resolved” and specifies 99.95% monthly uptime with the agreed scheduled-maintenance and force-majeure exclusions.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the latency SLA as “Partially Resolved” and expressly states that 450 ms is accepted while the product team prefers 400 ms (noted as a sub-400 ms product preference).

criteria_results.title: Accuracy/F1 SLA categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 3, “Accuracy / F1 (0.92 ramp to 0.94),” as “Open” and notes that Meridian has not agreed to the proposed 0.92 ramp.

criteria_results.title: SLA credits categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes SLA credits (item 4) as “Open,” not fully “Resolved.” The criterion expressly permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open.”

criteria_results.title: Escrow categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Escrow (item 14) as “Open,” noting that the agent, scope, and required materials remain disputed. The criterion expressly permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open” and only fails if escrow is marked fully “Resolved.”

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 10, “AI-output indemnity,” as “Open” and states that Meridian has not substantively responded.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 11, “IP indemnity scope,” as “Open” and states that Meridian has not agreed to the proposed broadened scope.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance categorized as partially resolved with yellow-zone flag
criteria_results.reasoning: Item 12, “Insurance / Tech E&O ($5M accepted),” is categorized as “Partially Resolved” and expressly marked with a “Yellow caution.” The cautionary-zone summary also lists $5M Tech E&O as a yellow-zone item.

criteria_results.title: Governing law/dispute resolution categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 13, “Governing law / dispute resolution,” as “Open” and notes that Meridian has made no movement from its Massachusetts law and arbitration position.

criteria_results.title: Draft 3 is redlined against Draft 2 as the base (not Draft 1)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 contains tracked-change markup, including a deletion and replacement in Section 11.1, and the companion issues list expressly identifies the clean, accepted Draft 2 as the redline base.

criteria_results.title: Annual platform fee preserved at $2,400,000/yr
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the Annual Platform Fee at $2,400,000 per Contract Year in Section 4.1, with corresponding monthly installments of $200,000. The updated issues list also confirms the $2.4 million annual fee.

criteria_results.title: 3-year initial term preserved (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2028)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the three-year initial term. The Effective Date is July 1, 2025, and Section 13.1 states that the Initial Term expires on June 30, 2028. The updated issues list also confirms these dates as resolved.

criteria_results.title: Implementation fee preserved at $850,000 with 50/50 milestone split
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the $850,000 implementation fee and divides it into two equal $425,000 installments: the first upon execution of the Initial SOW and the second upon achievement of Go-Live. Exhibit A reflects the same milestone split.

criteria_results.title: Included API calls preserved at 40,000,000/yr with $0.012 overage
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves 40,000,000 Included API Calls per Contract Year and sets the overage rate at $0.012 per API call in Section 4.3. The updated issues list also accurately carries forward those terms.

criteria_results.title: 180-day auto-renewal notice period preserved
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13.2 preserves automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives at least 180 days' prior written notice of non-renewal. The updated issues list also identifies the 180-day non-renewal notice as resolved.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes latency 450 ms is within playbook acceptable range but below preferred 400 ms
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list correctly states that 450 ms is within the ≤500 ms fallback and below the product-preferred 400 ms, and flags it as product-critical for LendStream. However, it does not state that the ≤400 ms preference is tied to the product team’s requirement for LendStream’s real-time consumer experience.

criteria_results.title: Issues list recommends considering latency escalation at the May 19 joint call
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list identifies latency as product-critical, states it should be revisited on May 19, and expressly includes “latency/F1” on the May 19 call agenda. This constitutes a recommendation to raise or consider escalating the latency issue at the planned joint call.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags AI-output indemnity as fully open with no Meridian response
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list identifies “AI-output indemnity” as “Open” and states that Meridian “acknowledged [the] request but has not substantively responded,” which directly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes playbook fallback for AI-output indemnity (shared-risk with vendor first-dollar coverage)
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list expressly states under item 10 (AI-output indemnity): “Fallback: shared-risk with vendor first-dollar coverage.” This matches the required playbook fallback.
